title: A cast between struct types pairs the fields by position and ignores the names; a different field count is an analysis error
description: Spark casts a struct to another struct type field by field in position order and takes the target's names. `CAST(named_struct('a', 100000, 'b', 1S) AS STRUCT<b: INT, a: INT>)` is `{b: 100000, a: 1}`, a rename (`STRUCT<x: INT, y: INT>`) keeps the values in order, and a nested struct is paired the same way at every level (`STRUCT<x: INT, y: STRUCT<q, r>>` of `(a, b: (c, d))` is `{x: 1, y: {q: 2, r: 3}}`). A target with another field count (a missing or an extra field) fails at analysis, `DATATYPE_MISMATCH.CAST_WITHOUT_SUGGESTION`, and so does a position whose types cannot be cast (a nested reorder that puts a struct where an INT is). Each field is cast by the scalar cast of its types: an overflow raises `CAST_OVERFLOW` under ANSI, wraps without it (100000 to SMALLINT is -31072), and `TRY_CAST` turns it into NULL for that field.
The same SQL gives other values on DuckDB and Polars, which pair by name (`duckdb-struct-cast-by-name`, `polars-struct-cast-by-name`).
reference: The core's struct kind carries no field names; a struct cast is refused at 1.0 (ruling 186) and a cast of a list of structs between the same field kinds is the identity, refused by #2376. Substrait's struct type has no field names (names belong to a schema's `NamedStruct`), so a cast between two struct types is positional by construction.
verdict: Spark pairs struct-cast fields by position; the three engines agree only where the target keeps the source's order and names.

provenance.checked_by: session for #2376, pyspark 4.3.0 local[1] on macOS arm64, ansi on and off

evidence.sql: SELECT CAST(s AS STRUCT<b: INT, a: INT>) FROM t  -- s = named_struct('a', 100000, 'b', 1S)
SELECT CAST(s AS STRUCT<x: INT, y: INT>) FROM t
SELECT CAST(s AS STRUCT<b: SMALLINT, a: SMALLINT>) FROM t
SELECT TRY_CAST(s AS STRUCT<b: SMALLINT, a: SMALLINT>) FROM t
SELECT CAST(s AS STRUCT<a: INT, b: SMALLINT, c: INT>) FROM t
SELECT CAST(s AS STRUCT<a: INT>) FROM t
SELECT CAST(s AS STRUCT<x: INT, y: STRUCT<q: INT, r: INT>>) FROM n  -- s = (a: 1, b: (c: 2, d: 3))
SELECT CAST(s AS STRUCT<b: STRUCT<d: INT, c: INT>, a: INT>) FROM n
